content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to the forum. I recently purchased a [product_name] unit and am trying to install [product_name] [version_no] on my Mac running OS X Catalina (10.15.4). The DVD isn't functioning properly and won't begin installation. Attempted copying files from the DVD to my hard drive, but that didn't resolve the issue. Is [product_name] [version_no] a 64-bit app? Will it work on MacOS Catalina (10.15.4)? I appreciate any help in advance. [user_name]
Did you review the previous post and download as well as read the PDF document mentioned?

Supported operating systems are listed in the documentation accompanying the DVD and the [product_name] manual: [product_name] [version_no] is compatible with: ● 32/64-bit Windows 7, 8, XP, and 10 ● 32/64-bit SUSE Linux 11.3 SP3, kernel 3.0.76 ● Mac OS X versions 10.7 through 10.11.
Hello, I'm interested in running it on Catalina as well. Did you end up finding a solution or workaround?

Did you check the post above yours? It's an official statement from [company_name]. Only the Mac OS versions listed are officially tested by [company_name]. For unlisted Mac OS versions, there is no support available.

It might be a bit late, but there's a solution that does require payment. You can install VMware Fusion and run a supported version of OS X within it. Alternatively, you can use Crossover (WINE) to run the Windows version under MacOS; this also costs but is effective.

Even though MacOS Catalina 10.15.4 isn't listed as supported, [product_name] [version_no] runs fine for me. I initially installed the software on an older MacOS and then migrated to Catalina, which makes me think the issue is only with the installer. I hope this information helps.
Thank you, that's very helpful. As a new Mac user, I'm learning as I go. I've considered Bootcamp or Parallels to run Solidworks CAD, and hope [product_name] runs well on these too. Thanks again.
Thanks, that's insightful. I just updated my machine to Catalina before starting this search, so I missed the opportunity to migrate like you did! Many thanks for your support. Cheers.

analysis.insight_summary: Users working to install [product_name] [version_no] on MacOS Catalina are experiencing installer issues due to lack of official support. While documentation from [company_name] only lists older MacOS versions as compatible, some users have succeeded through migration from previous OS versions or using virtualization/compatibility tools. These unofficial solutions can be complex or require payment, revealing a gap in compatibility with newer MacOS releases, which has led to user confusion and extra effort.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect official support and easy installation of [product_name] [version_no] on MacOS Catalina. They hope for 64-bit compatibility to match recent MacOS requirements.
pain_keywords: lack of official support for newest MacOS
